findings.field: Apply for Food Stamps in These Steps
findings.quote: A SNAP calculator or screener result does not file an application, and neither does a form that did not come from your state agency.

findings.field: Can I apply for food stamps over the phone?
findings.quote: You can call your state's toll-free SNAP Information hotline to reach the agency, and the eligibility interview is typically done by telephone or in person. The federal pages do not list phone as a filing method, so ask your state agency which submission methods your state accepts.
findings.replacement: Your state agency decides which submission methods it accepts. Ask [your state SNAP agency](https://fns-prod.azureedge.us/snap/state-directory) whether you can file by telephone, and keep the filing confirmation. The eligibility interview is typically completed by telephone or in person.
findings.defect: Original answer describes contact/interview and narrates which methods researchers did not find. Distinguish filing from interviewing and route the unresolved state-specific method to the official agency; do not assert nationwide phone filing availability or prohibition.

findings.field: Who can apply for food stamps?
findings.quote: FNA notes on its [eligibility page](https://fns-prod.azureedge.us/snap/recipient/eligibility) that the Working Families Tax Cuts change certain eligibility factors, including work requirements and non-citizen eligibility, and that it is updating the page.
findings.replacement: The [Working Families Tax Cuts Act](https://fns-prod.azureedge.us/snap/recipient/eligibility) changed SNAP work requirements and non-citizen eligibility. FNA is updating its [eligibility page](https://fns-prod.azureedge.us/snap/recipient/eligibility) for those changes.
findings.defect: First named law is unlinked and its name lacks Act. Link the actual primary agency warning and split the source/law/changes/update stack without adding exemption details.
